```{r}
#| label: setup

library(plotly)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## Popularity: Molly vs. Olivia (Today's Top Female Name)

```{r}
#| label: name-comparison

# Read baby name files and extract the year from the filename
files <- list.files("data", pattern = "^yob.*\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

babies <- read_csv(
  files,
  id = "file",
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "n"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(year = parse_number(basename(file)))

# Identify today's most popular female name in the latest year
latest_year <- max(babies$year)
top_female_today <- babies |>
  filter(year == latest_year, sex == "F") |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1) |>
  pull(name)

# Filter both names for the last 50 years and aggregate counts
comp_data <- babies |>
  filter(name %in% c("Molly", top_female_today), year >= 1976) |>
  group_by(name, year) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0("Name: ", name, "\nYear: ", year, "\nBabies: ", comma(n)))

# Create expanding frames so lines trace forward through time
comp_anim <- comp_data |>
  crossing(frame = unique(comp_data$year)) |>
  filter(year <= frame)

# Show birth milestone once the animation reaches 2008
birth_point <- comp_anim |>
  filter(name == "Molly", year == 2008)

birth_label <- comp_anim |>
  filter(name == "Molly", year == 2008) |>
  mutate(
    n = n + 550,
    label = "When I was born\n↓"
  )

# Build animated side-by-side comparison
p <- ggplot(comp_anim, aes(x = year, y = n, color = name, text = tooltip, frame = frame, group = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = birth_point, aes(x = year, y = n), color = "#e7298a", size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = birth_label,
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#e7298a",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.5,
    vjust = 0
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Olivia" = "#1b9e77", "Molly" = "#2b5c8f")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2020, by = 10), limits = c(1976, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Popularity Trend: Molly vs.", top_female_today, "(1976–2025)"),
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Interactive animated plot with Play/Pause controls
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  animation_opts(frame = 90, transition = 0, redraw = FALSE) |>
  animation_slider(currentvalue = list(prefix = "Year: "))
```

Today's most popular female name is **Olivia** (13,554 babies in 2025). While both names started at comparable levels in 1976 (around 1,200 to 1,700 babies), Molly peaked early in 1991, whereas Olivia surged dramatically starting in the late 1990s and has stayed near the top of the charts ever since.
